newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas farm activity increases in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas farm activity increases in latest week.

text.p: Farmers had six days suitable for hay cutting, soybean planting, wheat harvesting and rice flooding, rice fertilization and herbicide applications, acccording to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service update.
The previous week's fieldwork was limited to four days by stormy conditions.

Soybeans were 87 percent planted, up from 76 percent a week ago and down slightly from 89 percent for a year ago and the five-year average. Emergence was 77 percent, compared with 68 percent the previous week, 80 percent a year ago and 76 percent on average.
Wheat was harvested on 71 percent of the acreage, compared with 37 percent the previous week, 89 percent a year ago and the average of 88 percent.
Rice condition was rated 20 percent excellent, 54 percent good, 23 percent fair and three percent poor.
Cotton boll setting was zero, compared with 11 percent a year ago and the average of four percent. Cotton squaring was 61 percent, compared with 94 percent a year ago and 79 percent for the average.
Cotton condition was rated two percent excellent, 38 percent good, 51 percent fair and nine percent poor.
Soil moisture supplies were one percent very short, 34 percent short, 59 percent adequate and six percent surplus.
